title: Flat affine-base projection formula for algebraic spaces
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces and schemes are [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme]. Use the small etale site with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the full subcategory whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a flat quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces, and let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Flatness is tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]; quasi-compact means, as the target is affine, that every etale covering of $X$ has a finite subcovering (equivalently $|X|$ is quasi-compact), and quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. For an $A$-module $N$, let $F_N=\mathcal O_X\otimes_A N$ be the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $F_N$ is quasi-coherent, the assignment $N\mapsto F_N$ is exact, and its derived pullback is represented by $F_N[0]$. Write $R\Gamma(X,-)$ for the unbounded right derived functor of global sections [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], valued in $D(A)$ through $A\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Derived tensor is computed using K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The canonical projection morphism is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$,
$$R\Gamma(X,E)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}F_N[0]).$$
Regard $f$ as a morphism of ringed topoi of small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with derived functors $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ computed by K-flat, resp. K-injective, resolutions. The projection morphism is the adjoint of the map obtained by pulling back $R f_*E$ and applying the counit $L f^*R f_*E\to E$, tensored with $L f^*N$. Its naturality includes every homomorphism $N\to N\prime$ of $A$-modules. Spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 08IN, lemma-cohomology-base-change, specialized to an affine base and modules in degree zero; the flat-pullback convention is the paragraph preceding lemma-check-quasi-coherence-on-covering.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and write $a_A$ for the affine etale associated-module functor. The pullback of $a_A(N)$ is $F_N$: on an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$, both are the etale associated sheaf of $B\otimes_A N$. Indeed, the Zariski/etale comparison identifies the chart pullback with ordinary scheme pullback, and its affine-sections formula is $n\otimes b\mapsto b f^*n$. These formulas commute with chart restrictions by the tensor balancing relation, so identify the sheaves and their maps. Thus $F_N$ is quasi-coherent by preservation of quasi-coherence under space pullback. Since $f$ is flat on scheme charts, the affine criterion makes $B$ flat over $A$. Flat tensor exactness makes $B\otimes_A-$ exact. The affine associated-module equivalence therefore shows that every short exact sequence of $A$-modules gives a short exact sequence of the $F_N$ on each chart. Exactness of sheaves is local: a local kernel element lifts on a chart and these local lifts give the required sheaf epimorphism onto the kernel. Hence $H:N\mapsto F_N$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 08IN, affine specialization; paragraph preceding lemma-check-quasi-coherence-on-covering; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03GA; algebra.tex Tag 00HD.

proof.text: Let $p_Y:(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_Y)\to(*,A)$ be the global-sections ringed-topos morphism and $p_X=p_Yf$. Its module pullback is $H$ on $X$ and $a_A$ on $Y$: a map $\mathcal O_X\otimes_A N\to M$ is equivalent to the $A$-linear map $N\to\Gamma(X,M)$ sending $n$ to the image of $1\otimes n$, with inverse $b\otimes n\mapsto b\,u(n)$. This proves the adjunction and identifies the structural action. The exact-functor derived-factorization theorem applied to $H$ shows $Lp_X^*N[0]=F_N[0]$. Moreover $Lf^*a_A(K)=Lp_X^*K$ for every $K\in D(A)$: choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ of $K$; pullback to $Y$ preserves that resolving class, and iterated scalar extension is identified with composite extension by $b\otimes(c\otimes x)\mapsto bc\otimes x$. In particular $Lf^*a_A(N[0])=F_N[0]$.

source.place: Tag 08IN, canonical map; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 07A4 and 0G7E; exact flat-pullback paragraph preceding lemma-check-quasi-coherence-on-covering.

proof.text: Record the affine tensor dictionary, including its map. The equivalence $a_A:D(A)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y_{\mathrm{et}})$ has quasi-inverse $R\Gamma(Y,-)$. As $a_A=Lp_Y^*$, the canonical pullback tensor comparison gives $a_A(P\otimes_A^L Q)\simeq a_A(P)\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^L a_A(Q)$. For $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ put $P=R\Gamma(Y,M)$ and use its canonical counit $a_A(P)\simeq M$. Applying the inverse equivalence gives $R\Gamma(Y,M)\otimes_A^L Q\simeq R\Gamma(Y,M\otimes^L a_A(Q))$. This is the projection mate for $p_Y$: after applying the fully faithful $a_A$, its defining adjunct is precisely the tensor comparison followed by that counit. Thus it is the specified canonical map, natural in both arguments, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of their values.

source.place: Tag 08IN, affine equivalence paragraph; Tag 071Q (lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 07A4, 07A6 and 0B56.

proof.text: Both $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $Y$: for $X$ this is the given qcqs morphism, and for $Y$ it is the identity. The space pushforward-right-adjoint theorem gives $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ with a right adjoint. Hence $Rf_*$ preserves set-indexed coproducts by the left-adjoint colimit theorem. These are the ambient derived coproducts by the stated coproduct clause of space perfect localizing generation, applied to $X$ and $Y$. Derived tensor with a fixed object preserves coproducts as a left adjoint by the ringed-site closed tensor theorem and the same colimit theorem; this applies also to the one-point ringed site defining $D(A)$. The functor $Lf^*$ preserves coproducts by its derived adjunction, and $a_A$ does so as an equivalence. Finally $Lf^*a_A(Q)$ and $E\otimes^L Lf^*a_A(Q)$ have quasi-coherent cohomology by the space derived-pullback/tensor theorem. Thus every coproduct in these composites stays in the subcategories where preservation by $Rf_*$ is available.

source.place: Tag 08IN, direct-sum paragraph; Tag 08FB (lemma-quasi-coherence-pushforward-direct-sums). The already existing right-adjoint input gives exactly this preservation via adjunction, as in spaces-duality.tex Tag 0E55; no projection formula is used to obtain it.

proof.text: Fix $E$. For $Q\in D(A)$ define $T(Q)=Rf_*E\otimes^L a_A(Q)$ and $U(Q)=Rf_*(E\otimes^L Lf^*a_A(Q))$. Use the canonical transformation $\alpha_Q:T(Q)\to U(Q)$ whose adjunct is $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\mu_{Rf_*E,a_A(Q)}$. The exact projection-mate theorem says these functors are exact and this transformation commutes with shifts and with connecting arrows of distinguished triangles. Precomposition by $a_A$ preserves exactness because $a_A$ is induced termwise by an exact functor, by exact derived factorization. Step 4 shows $T,U$ preserve all set-indexed coproducts. At $Q=A[0]$, $a_A(Q)=\mathcal O_Y[0]$ and the unit normalization in the exact projection-mate theorem gives $\alpha_{A[0]}=1_{Rf_*E}$. Shift compatibility then makes every $\alpha_{A[k]}$ invertible.

source.place: Tag 08IN, canonical adjunction construction, direct sums and triangles, and final shifts-of-structure-sheaf sentence.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the isomorphism locus of $\alpha$. It contains every $A[k]$ by Step 5. It is closed under distinguished-triangle two-out-of-three by the triangle-comparison theorem, since the required connecting square was supplied in Step 5. It is closed under coproducts: under the comparisons of Step 4, naturality with every coprojection identifies $\alpha_{\bigoplus Q_i}$ with $\bigoplus\alpha_{Q_i}$, whose inverse is the sum of the inverses. It is closed under retracts: for $Q\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{r}Q$, $ri=1$, an inverse of $\alpha_Q$ is $T(r)\alpha_P^{-1}U(i)$; the two inverse equations follow by naturality and $ri=1$. It is closed under isomorphisms by naturality. Apply derived-module free generation to conclude $\mathcal C=D(A)$. This is generation of the entire unbounded derived category, not an induction on the length of a bounded resolution.

Take $Q=N[0]$ in Step 6 and apply $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ to $\alpha_Q$. Its source is $R\Gamma(X,E)\otimes_A^L N[0]$ by Step 3 and the canonical derived direct-image composition comparison for $p_Yf$. Its target is $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^L F_N[0])$ by Step 2 and that same composition comparison. This yields an isomorphism in $D(A)$ with exactly the asserted objects. To check the arrow, the projection-composition identity reads $\pi_{p_Yf}=Rp_{Y,*}(\pi_f)\circ\pi_{p_Y}$ under those comparisons. The first factor is the image of $\alpha_Q$ and the second is exactly the affine tensor dictionary of Step 3. Thus the displayed arrow is the canonical counit-defined projection morphism. All comparisons and both projection factors are natural in $Q$ and $E$. In particular every homomorphism $N\to N'$ gives the stated naturality square, with the actual map $F_N\to F_{N'}$ of Step 1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q36-a81ae5b21 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the item and every cited node in full, with no fixes needed. The delivery adds a 7-step proof to the item and creates no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and correct. The proof follows Stacks spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08IN (lemma-cohomology-base-change, lines 4662-4720), which I read: (1) on affine étale charts Spec B, F_N = f^*a_A(N) is the sheaf of B⊗_A N, so F_N is quasi-coherent, and N -> F_N is exact because A->B is flat. (2) Lp_X^*N[0] = F_N[0] by exact derived factorization, and Lf^*a_A = Lp_X^* through flat-term K-flat resolutions. (3) Through the equivalence D(A) ≃ D_QCoh(Spec A_et), the projection mate for p_Y is an isomorphism, with the counit and unit identified. (4) Rf_* preserves coproducts on D_QCoh because it has a right adjoint (Tag 0E55), and D_QCoh coproducts are the ambient ones; Lf^*, tensor and a_A also preserve coproducts. (5) The mate node gives exactness, shift compatibility and α_{R_Y}=1, so α is an isomorphism at every A[k]. (6) The isomorphism locus is closed under triangles, coproducts and retracts (I checked the explicit inverse), so free generation gives all of D(A). (7) Apply RΓ and the composition identity π_{p_Y f}=Rp_Y*(π_f)∘π_{p_Y}; this identifies the canonical arrow, natural in N->N'. No circularity: 0E55 uses 08DU, Bondal-van den Bergh (line 3674) and 08FB (line 646), all before 08IN, and the DAG closure (1422 nodes) has no cycle. Duplicate search over dag/nodes for 08IN and projection formula found only scheme-level nodes (lem-pc-qcqs-derived-projection-mate and others), the base-change node lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change and the user node lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-pullback-limit, so no duplicate exists. lean.statement: theorem space_affine_derived_projection_formula (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec A)) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec A)))) (hflat : MapIsFlat f) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f.hom.hom)) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] : ∃ d : AffineProjectionData A X, (∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A, (X.smallModuleEquivalence.inverse.obj (affineScalarSheaf A X N)).IsQuasicoherent) ∧ (∀ (E : X.DerivedQCoh) (N : ModuleCat.{u} A), IsIso (affineDerivedProjectionMap A X d E.obj N)) ∧ (∀ (E E' : X.DerivedQCoh) (e : E ⟶ E') (N N' : ModuleCat.{u} A) (n : N ⟶ N'), (tensor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))).map (Prod.mkHom ((affineProjectionRGamma A X d.G d.sections_additive).map e.hom) ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map n)) ≫ affineDerivedProjectionMap A X d E'.obj N' = affineDerivedProjectionMap A X d E.obj N ≫ (affineProjectionRGamma A X d.G d.sections_additive).map ((affineProjectionTensor A X).map (Prod.mkHom e.hom ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.SmallModules 0).map (affineScalarSheafMap A X n)))))
